title: Beatrix and the Harvest
premise: Pest controller Jonah Blackwood is called to Hollowmere Farm, where the founders' descendants report a voice in the walls that answers questions—and her own decade of suppressed memories begins surfacing in the recordings. She learns she was one of the children the founders used to seal something beneath the farm, and that the seal is failing because the ritual requires a willing participant who remembers. As the entity wears the faces of people she's lost and the town closes ranks to protect its founding secret, Jonah must choose between destroying the evidence that would expose the town's crimes or completing the harvest ritual with herself as the offering. In the end she tricks the entity into consuming a recording of the truth instead of her memory, freeing the farm but leaving her unable to recall whether she ever had a daughter.
about_author: Dominic Almeida is the pen name of a former rural insurance adjuster who spent years documenting claims in farming communities where certain houses were always struck from the ledger. He writes horror about paperwork, property lines, and the things that live in the gaps between them.

chapters.title: The Callout
chapters.summary: Jonah Blackwood takes a routine pest call at Hollowmere Farm, noting claw marks too high for any animal and scratches arranged like writing. POV: Jonah. The beat is professional detachment cracking into unease as the client, Ruth Ellery, asks if Jonah has 'been here before.'

chapters.title: Fingerprints
chapters.summary: Inspecting the cellar, Jonah finds handprints pressed into the mortar—small ones, child-sized, decades old yet dust-free. She sets recording equipment before leaving. POV: Jonah. The emotional beat is denial; she catalogs rational explanations aloud like a prayer.

chapters.title: Playback
chapters.summary: Reviewing overnight audio, Jonah hears a second voice answering questions no one asked aloud—questions about her. She returns to the farm uninvited. POV: Jonah. The beat is dread sharpening into compulsion; she needs to know what it knows.

chapters.title: Ruth
chapters.summary: Ruth Ellery admits the voice predates her family and shows Jonah a founder's ledger listing 'harvests' every forty years—the last dated ten years ago. POV: alternating Jonah/Ruth. The beat is reluctant alliance between two women keeping different secrets.

chapters.title: Ten Years Quiet
chapters.summary: Triggered by the ledger, Jonah recalls fragments: a farmhouse kitchen, other children, a man counting them like livestock. POV: Jonah, in fractured flashback. The beat is vertigo—her decade of 'explanations' was engineered forgetting.

chapters.title: The Other Survivors
chapters.summary: Jonah tracks down two other former children: one catatonic, one hostile and wealthy, Dana Voss, who warns her to stop digging. POV: Jonah/Dana. The beat is fear wearing the mask of threat; Dana knows exactly what's waking up.

chapters.title: It Knows My Name
chapters.summary: The voice begins speaking to Jonah directly through the farm's intercom system, using her childhood nickname only one dead person knew. POV: Jonah. The beat is intimate terror—the entity isn't haunting the house; it's haunting her.

chapters.title: Founders' Chapel
chapters.summary: In the collapsed chapel, Jonah finds murals of children walking into the earth smiling, and a ritual text describing an exchange: memory given willingly, the thing below kept fed. POV: Jonah. The beat is horrified understanding—consent is the mechanism.

chapters.title: The Town Closes Ranks
chapters.summary: Jonah brings her findings to the county sheriff and local historian; both stonewall, and her truck is vandalized within hours. POV: Jonah/interludes from townsfolk. The beat is isolation—justice here means silence, maintained for generations.

chapters.title: Dana's Confession
chapters.summary: Dana reveals the last harvest failed because the chosen child—Jonah—ran, and the entity has been starving since, growing crueler. POV: Dana. The beat is guilt weaponized; Dana helped catch her back then.

chapters.title: The Daughter Question
chapters.summary: Jonah discovers records suggesting she had a daughter during her missing decade—a girl placed for adoption by someone with power over her. POV: Jonah. The beat is grief braided with rage; even her love may have been curated.

chapters.title: Voices in the Walls
chapters.summary: The entity escalates, mimicking the voices of the other harvested children begging Jonah to finish it. Ruth's husband is found hollow-eyed and mute. POV: multiple, converging on the farm. The beat is siege—the house is feeding now.

chapters.title: What the Recordings Keep
chapters.summary: Analyzing ten years of her own old sleep recordings, Jonah finds the entity has been rehearsing her memories back to her nightly, keeping them alive against her will. POV: Jonah. The beat is terrible gratitude—it preserved what the town tried to erase.

chapters.title: The Historian's Archive
chapters.summary: The town historian, dying and afraid, gives Jonah the original founding covenant naming every harvested child—including Jonah's mother. POV: Jonah/historian. The beat is inheritance of sin; this predates her and will outlast her unless broken.

chapters.title: Ruth's Choice
chapters.summary: Ruth offers herself as the harvest to spare Jonah, revealing the Ellerys have supplied offerings for six generations. POV: Ruth. The beat is loyalty versus truth—devotion built on atrocity.

chapters.title: Descent Preparation
chapters.summary: Jonah studies the ritual and realizes the entity consumes memory, not flesh—and that a recorded truth might substitute for a lived one. POV: Jonah. The beat is cold clarity; she stops being prey and starts planning.

chapters.title: They Come for Her
chapters.summary: Dana and the town elders attempt to take Jonah to the pit by force; Ruth turns on her own family to stop them, and Dana dies in the struggle. POV: action-driven ensemble. The beat is the cost of secrets made flesh and blood.

chapters.title: Into the Earth
chapters.summary: Jonah descends through the founders' tunnel carrying recordings of everything: the covenant, the confessions, her daughter's name. The entity greets her wearing her mother's face. POV: Jonah. The beat is calm at the edge of annihilation.

chapters.title: The Harvest Reversed
chapters.summary: Jonah offers the recordings instead of her mind; the entity feeds on documented truth and chokes on it, unraveling as the town's buried crimes surface in its scream. POV: Jonah. The beat is climax—justice outside the law, delivered underground.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: The farm caves inward; Jonah barely escapes as Ruth chooses to stay behind with the dying thing, ending her family's covenant personally. POV: Jonah/Ruth. The beat is sacrifice without absolution.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: The recordings go public; the town must reckon with its founding. Jonah searches for her daughter and finds an address, a life, a stranger. POV: Jonah. The beat is bittersweet accountability—truth costs everything it saves.

chapters.title: What Remains
chapters.summary: Months later, Jonah listens to her final sleep recording and hears, faintly, her own younger voice saying her daughter's name—one memory the entity returned. She drives toward the address. POV: Jonah. The beat is earned, fragile hope.
